📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that after a full season of cutthroat legal proceedings, War's central divorce trial between actor Carla Duval (Sienna Miller) and tech mogul Morgan Henderson (Dominic West) has reached its final verdict. The winner? No one. But the loser? Also no one.

That's because, after some eleventh-hour heroics from mole Johnny Warren (Archie Renaux) and honeypot Flora Monroe (Rose Williams), Carla and Morgan reach their own settlement, independent of their lawyers and the judge. Following their decision, Carla will receive 50 percent of Zephyr's shares and monthly payments from Morgan until he retires. Carla and Morgan will share custody of Carla's son, Gabe (Aran Murphy). In short, it's basically what Carla had been asking for this whole time, and what the pair could have achieved without going to court.

Industry observers note that their decision stems from hearing Flora read Morgan's conciliatory letter to Carla, which St. John Smallwood (Pip Torrens) tried to dispose of, aloud in court. For Carla and Morgan, the letter is a reminder of the good in their relationship, something they sorely needed to recall after months of highly public mud-slinging.

In a recent development, "It tied itself up with humanity and kindness, and that was unexpected for me when I was reading it," Miller told Mashable in a junket interview alongside West. "I think the moral of that being that had these two people dropped their ego and their pride and nasty covetousness, if they'd let all of that go, they could have probably resolved this without the hideous experience of taking each other to court.".

"It felt like a spectacular waste of $10 million on lawyers' fees," West joked.

For series creator George Kay, there was never a version of War Season 1 where the court ruled in favor of one side or the other.

In a recent development, "In the majority of these major divorces, the real winners are the lawyers, and so we wanted to take that agency away from the justice system and put it back in the hands of [Carla and Morgan]," Kay told Mashable in a junket interview. "So, it was always going to be down to them to work it out, which is the big expensive irony of what they've been through.".

Industry observers note that by the end of Season 1, Carla and Morgan have found what seems to be an affectionate alliance. Even though Carla now has the Zephyr shares she asked for, she won't be using them against Morgan to trigger the sale to Michael Ancker (David Menkin), as Zephyr CEO Gillian Pope (Angel Coulby) wanted. Instead, Gillian is being ousted, as it turns out she leaked the security footage of Flora leaving Morgan's hotel room to the press.

In War's final scene between Carla and Morgan, the pair stand, at peace, on a Normandy beach by their cottage.

"I'll always love you," Morgan tells Carla.

As it seems that the pair is about to go their separate ways, Carla calls Morgan back up to the cottage for a hot chocolate with Gabe. It's proof that their life as a pairing isn't over. It's just taken a different shape. And maybe thanks to that, both Carla and Morgan "won" in the trial after all.

"The end of a divorce, it's not like someone's dead," West noted. "You either never speak to each other again, run screaming through the streets, or you realize actually why you love the person in the first place. I think that's what happens to Morgan in the end.".

"We described this divorce at the world's most expensive couples therapy, because it's only by going through everything that they've been through, hearing what the other one thinks via their lawyers, emotionally reengaging with everything they've had in their relationship, that by the end they realize what an amazing thing they have, and so we leave them okay," Kay noted. "They're divorced, technically, but actually they're much better parents and they're much closer emotionally, and that was always a North Star for us.".

The sweet ending for Morgan and Carla is at odds with the rest of War's bloodthirsty, win-at-any-cost tone. But for Kay, that was intentional.

Industry observers note that "We didn't want it to be bleak or dark," Kay said of the ending. "We wanted it to be redemptive.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

OpenAI dropped two new AI models this week in the form of GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, each surpassing benchmarks of their predecessors, but people who have begun using them haven’t all walked away very happy.

Recent findings suggest that A new AI model seems to drop almost every couple of days from one of the big tech giants, each improving on the previous version in one way or another. However, OpenAI’s latest and greatest are getting some pushback from developers and early testers. For the everyday user, the 6.2 Sol and Astra should perform more than serviceably, but those looking to dig in, test and use the new models for more professional work may run into some hiccups they’re not used to, according to some feedback.

Recent findings suggest that ethan Mollick, associate professor and director of the Generative AI Lab at the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School of Business, said in a LinkedIn post that GPT-6.2 Astra was “harder to steer and work with,” and “frequently seemed ‘lazy’,” compared with competitor models. Another brutal assessment on LinkedIn came from Jason J. Fleagle, head of AI at NETSYNC: “I think GPT-6.2 has to be one of the worst AI models OpenAI has ever released.”.

Sources indicate that however, there might be more to the story than that. OpenAI Codex leader Thibault Sottiaux, known as Tibo, mentioned in an X post that early builds of 6.2 Sol and Astra were released to influencers some time ago, that updates and changes were made to the models within the past couple of days, and that he assumes no retesting was done since. Only time and more testing will show whether these improvements make much of a meaningful difference.

OpenAI didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.

Industry observers note that after we missed out on the Xiaomi 17 Pro and Pro Max last year, the Chinese smartphone giant is finally bringing its dual-screen flagships to the West. It's just debuted the fresh Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, and I would be pretty worried if I were a certain Cupertino-based competitor.

Both phones look like an all-round excellent package, with top-of-the-line specs including the brand-upcoming Snapdragon 8 Elite chipsets.

It has been revealed that the Xiaomi 18 Pro is the model for those after a more compact, but still powerful, phone, with its 6.4-inch 120Hz AMOLED front display and 6,000mAh battery. It's powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 chipset, paired with 12GB of RAM and either 256GB or 512GB of storage.

The Xiaomi 18 Pro Max, meanwhile, bumps the main screen size up to 6.9 inches and upgrades the chipset to the absolutely top-of-the-line Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 – presently the fastest Android SoC on the market. The base model offers 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, but there are also more expensive 12+512GB and 16+1TB versions available.

The bigger design also makes space for a much larger battery, which comes in at 7,050mAh with 100W wired HyperCharge support (the base 18 Pro, in contrast, only supports 90W wired HyperCharge).

The front displays of both phones support Xiaomi's newly introduced privacy display technology, which is effectively the tech giant's take on Samsung's Privacy Display feature and helps obscure sensitive information from prying eyes.

According to recent reports, both the 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max boast similar camera setups, with a 200MP main shooter and 200MP periscope telephoto lens alongside a 50MP ultra-wide. As with other recent Xiaomi devices, the cameras were co-engineered with Leica and offer a range of photo styles inspired by the camera maker.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

For me, the real highlight, however, is the innovative rear display situated on the back of both models. It offers a range of handy features, from controlling media playback to offering a real-time view of the cameras to make selfies easier.

You can fully customize it with a range of watch-like faces as well (including some options with cute 3D animal mascots) and even use generative AI to create your own apps right from the settings menu.

It's seriously cool and seems like a genuine reason to pick the 18 Pro or 18 Pro Max over other flagship models.

All of this doesn't exactly come cheap, however. The Xiaomi 18 Pro starts at £1,199 (that's roughly $1,600), and the 18 Pro Max starts at £1,399 (around $1,850) for the 12+256GB model.

They both come in four color options: Black, White, Velvet Red, and Cosmic Blue.

Tens of thousands of UK fridges secured from hackers in secret nationwide operation

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (893 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sweden was among countries to report a cyber incident in which some supermarket fridge units had been hiked up in temperature.
  • A behind the scenes cyber-security operation has taken place to secure tens of thousands of fridges and freezers at major UK supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations and stadiums from hackers, the BBC has learned.
  • Recent waves of cyber-attacks in Europe have seen tonnes of food spoiled at hundreds of stores, causing millions of pounds of damage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sweden was among countries to report a cyber incident in which some supermarket fridge units had been hiked up in temperature.

A behind the scenes cyber-security operation has taken place to secure tens of thousands of fridges and freezers at major UK supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants, petrol stations and stadiums from hackers, the BBC has learned.

Recent waves of cyber-attacks in Europe have seen tonnes of food spoiled at hundreds of stores, causing millions of pounds of damage.

France has blamed Iran for one of the waves of attacks that impacted its supermarkets, a claim Tehran denies.

It was thought the UK had largely escaped such hacks as the British refrigeration industry relies on different devices but there was in fact a potential vulnerability the sector has been rushing to fix.

In late October, security researchers discovered a major flaw that, if found by hackers, could have led to even worse damage to the UK.

Since then, researchers, IT teams and the National Cyber Security Centre have been working around the clock to warn dozens of companies.

The BBC has not reported on the large-scale, secretive operation until now to reduce the chances of hackers causing harm if they found the vulnerability.

The security threat was discovered by ethical hackers at a firm called Omega Systems - it was then verified and expanded upon by experts at Pen Test Partners who helped raise the alarm.

The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), the Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra) and Food Standards Agency (FSA) were then involved in the campaign to plug the security holes.

They held industry conference calls and tasked teams to contact firms at risk.

Thousands of devices controlling tens of thousands of refrigeration devices were taken off the open internet either remotely or, in some cases, physically - with staff ordered to remove internet cables and monitor temperatures manually.

BBC news has learnt most major supermarkets have been forced to divert IT teams to address the risks, with a worker at one large chain saying they took hundreds of devices offline every day over the course of a week.

"It did feel like a race against time as we were expecting another wave of these fridge hacks to come," remarked the person, who did not want to be publicly named.

Sources indicate that "From a business perspective it could have been potentially devastating with business interruption and supply chain problems. Our warehouses have millions of pounds worth of food that could have been spoiled if any hackers found out about this method of attack," they added.

There have been three waves of hacks on refrigeration temperature controllers so far this year:.

In August, fridges at a small number of US military bases were impacted.

On 11 and 12 October hundreds of supermarkets and food processing sites in France were hit when Danfoss temperature control systems were targeted.

According to recent reports, on 1 and 2 November dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries were hit, with Belgium and Luxembourg the worst affected. A small number of blood bank sites in France were also impacted.

The waves of attacks prompted an expert at Omega Solutions to examine the security of the most popular refrigeration controllers in the UK, made by British firm Resource Data Management (RDM).

RDM disputes the critical nature of the vulnerabilities exposed but has been praised for its professional response to address the concerns, the BBC understands.

As well as supermarkets, multiple other areas of UK food and beverage industry were also warned to take action about the risks.

These include convenience stores, petrol stations, restaurants and fast food chains, sports arenas, hotels, food processing plants and cold storage sites.

Each RDM controller can be used to remotely control the temperature of dozens of fridges and freezers.

"These popular controllers had a similar weak password problem to the Danfoss and other controllers that were attacked so successfully in previous hacks so we had to get the message out as soon as possible and keep it secret," noted Ken Munro of Pen Test Partners.

"There is so much extra attention on these ubiquitous bits of kit now that it was likely a matter of days until criminals or nation state hackers figured it out," he added.

RDM, though, states comparisons with the units attacked in mainland Europe are not fair because hacking their fridges and freezers would have involved getting hold of a piece of hardware.

The ethical hackers say this would have been achievable as the hardware in question can be purchased cheaply online on sites like eBay.

"This was a vulnerability identified in a test environment," said Ged Evans, CEO of RDM.

He stated the test "went beyond" what such exercises usually involved, as it "included dismantling our hardware".

"In any event we have acted at pace to address this issue and have already deployed first patch releases and have been in proactive contact with our customers to flag any challenges and recommend mitigatory steps," he added.

RDM confirmed that there was no sign of any malicious activity on the controllers and that it continued to work with the NCSC and other authorities to monitor the situation.

  • Sources indicate that nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.

According to recent reports, U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.).

Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure organization that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The Latest York Times has reported.

It has been revealed that the story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly stated, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.

It has been revealed that by early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the organization he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee.

The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.

As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.

Nvidia reported its quarterly earnings on Tuesday, which beat Wall Street expectations with $115.8 billion in revenue, up 103% year-over-year. Despite the unknowns the company faces without Huang involved, interim CEO Colette Kress said that full-year revenue is also on track to exceed expectations. The company also plans to raise its outlook for the 2028 fiscal year, indicating confidence that this unexpected leadership change won’t get in the way of its trajectory.

“We have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap,” Kress said. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual. We’ve engaged with our customers, we’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners. They’re all 100% behind us.”.

Nvidia chairman Harvey C. Jones affirmed that the company is not considering reinstating Huang. Kress also said that Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, ending the company’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country.

Jensen Huang posted his first public statement since he admitted to having an extramarital affair more than a week earlier.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he wrote.

Many of Huang’s colleagues in the tech industry, including Elon Musk, Anduril founder Palmer Luckey, and Y Combinator President and CEO Garry Tan, have called for his return.

Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an….

More reports continue to roll out that illustrate the shock and severity of Huang’s resignation from Nvidia.

Bloomberg reported that Huang looked “broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted” by the time he surrendered his role on Wednesday night, uttering phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.”.

Separately, The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang had been critical of his CFO and current interim CEO, Colette Kress. Huang is stated to have described Kress as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation this summer, and he had described Kress as someone who could not help him steer strategy or decision-making.

In a scathing letter sent to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Representative Richard Neal (D-MA) and Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) remarked they will investigate how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China, especially after Trump was briefed about Huang’s relationship with a purported Chinese spy.

Sources indicate that “Although [Lutnick] and President Trump were reportedly briefed on this intelligence, the Administration did not appear to acknowledge this evident national security threat. On the contrary: despite reportedly learning of Mr. Huang’s compromising relationship last fall, President Trump granted Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 AI chips to China in December 2025 in exchange for a cut of the export sales,” the letter states.

That same evening, Senator Tim Scott (R-SC) requested that Huang and Lutnick both testify before the Senate Banking Committee.

“The American people deserve answers,” Scott wrote on X.

After Huang was already ousted from Nvidia, we continued to learn more incriminating claims about the former CEO. According to Reuters, Huang had a third affair with an additional, unnamed employee of Nvidia.

Nvidia said its board had accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The firm’s current CFO, Colette Kress, will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang.

According to recent reports, harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993.

Later in the day, Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26.

“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very notable company to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast remarked to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”.

The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed.

Industry observers note that after reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly looks to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.

Recent findings suggest that huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has noted. The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.

The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.

According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.

According to recent reports, huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressmen to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed.

The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.

In a recent development, alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported. The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.

Sources indicate that nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported. Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.

In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.

On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and indicated support for the Nvidia CEO.

“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump noted.

When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia, Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”.

Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.

It has been revealed that “I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his firm. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”.

Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”.

“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our organization. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.

Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.

Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.

“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote. “The problem of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”.

Recent findings suggest that U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the Fresh York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.

An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.

Sources indicate that “Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo mentioned. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”.

In a recent development, U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the Fresh York Times.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.

In a recent development, around the same time, per the Upcoming York Times’ report, U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.

In a recent development, the Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump, has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.

Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports.

According to recent reports, megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service.

Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born.

These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told press that the firm did not have “any reason to believe products had been diverted.”.

“NVIDIA visited multiple Megaspeed sites yet again earlier this week and confirmed what we previously observed — Megaspeed is running a small commercial cloud, like many other companies throughout the world, as allowed by U.S. export control rules,” the Nvidia spokesperson stated at the time.

Last Monday, Apple released macOS 27.3 beta 2, with newly introduced privacy controls for Full Disk Access and automation tools, and the availability of Apple Intelligence in China.

Those came alongside several fresh features and tools on macOS 27.3 beta 1, including vertical tabs and adaptive dark mode in Safari, native Live Activities support, Markdown rendering in Quick Look, additional checks for potentially harmful content shared through iCloud links, and Siri AI support for Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

Industry observers note that and speaking of Siri AI, macOS 27.3 also expands the assistant’s capabilities across Apple’s own apps, allowing consumers to perform more complex actions in Messages, Music, Calendar, Photos, and Reminders, as well as manage files and folders. Apple is also introducing fresh tools for third-party developers to build more advanced Siri AI integrations using Markdown-based instructions.

While macOS 27.2 was a rather uneventful patch, macOS 27.3 is shaping up to be the biggest update since the release of macOS 27, and people on the public beta can now try out these new features ahead of their official release.

The release build for macOS 27.3 public beta 2 is 26C5047e, which matches the developer build.

GTA 6 central characters Lucia and Jason.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to have become the biggest entertainment launch in history following the blockbuster video game's debut on Thursday, after a 13-year wait.

The highly anticipated open-world action-adventure saw pre-orders and first day sales total more than 24.5 million units, raking in about $2.36bn (Â£1.8bn), according to analytics platform Sensor Tower.

In comparison, this year's highest grossing movie so far, Spider-Man: Brand Fresh Day, made $2.5bn over its entire run in cinemas.

GTA 6's maker Rockstar and parent company Take-Two have not released details of the game's sales but said demand has been "unprecedented". The BBC has contacted both the firms for comment.

The game is the latest instalment in Rockstar's nearly three decade old crime simulator franchise, which has become one of the most popular games in history.

At its core, the series is a satirical take on the American dream, putting players in the shoes of career criminals in Leonida, the game's Florida-inspired state.

The latest release follows fresh characters Lucia and her partner Jason, a pair of small-time criminals.

GTA 6 is estimated to have cost more than $1bn to develop, which would make it the most expensive video game in history.

GTA 6 gets 'near perfect' reviews as game launches.

Sensor Tower mentioned GTA 6 will be so popular that it will reduce the time gamers spend on other single-player titles by 10%.

The research firm mentioned its estimates are based on email receipts data and other statistical sources that track millions of people daily. They also track public profiles across major gaming platforms like PlayStation and Xbox, where GTA 6 is available.

Around three quarters of the game's sales have been for the PlayStation 5 and the balance on Xbox, Sensor Tower said.

Niko Partners, a gaming market research firm, stated it expects GTA 6 to make more than $3bn in sales worldwide this year.

That figure would rank GTA 6 among the highest-grossing entertainment releases ever, but it would still have some way to go to catch 1939's Gone with the Wind, which has made an estimated $4.5bn, adjusted for inflation.

Rockstar is expected to make even more money from GTA 6 over the coming years.

The Latest York-based studio has yet to announce when the game will be released for PCs or given a date for its multiplayer expansion, which will allow players to interact and go on missions with others over the internet.

If 2013's GTA 5 is any guide, multiplayer will add dozens more hours of gameplay and bring in even more revenue for Rockstar as players spend real money on in-game property, cars and other perks.

GTA 6 launched around the world on 19 November.

Anticipation for the blockbuster title has grown through repeated delays, following a 13-year wait.

GTA 6 has been hailed by some reviewers as one of the most impressive gaming experiences ever. Entertainment media site IGN described it as an "uncompromisingly engineered" masterpiece.

The release of GTA 6 at midnight on Thursday across various time zones saw many gamers stay up through the night, while some took the following day off to play.

Its launch broke Virgin Media O2's evening traffic record as people rushed to install GTA 6's huge 212GB file on consoles.

The game's graphic content has resulted in censorship in Japan and, like earlier GTA releases, is not approved for sale in mainland China.

Meta Is Trying to Woo Teens to Instagram Through Schools

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (792 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, meta has justifiably attracted more scrutiny than ever this year, along with multibillion-dollar judgments and settlements, over how its business practices affect young social media users.
  • In fact, the tech giant has made a major push toward drawing teenagers to one of its flagship platforms, Instagram, by targeting them at their schools.
  • According to documents obtained and reported by NPR, Meta released an initiative called Project Gryffindor, named after a Hogwarts house in the Harry Potter series, to create school communities on Instagram in order to boost user counts and engagement on the platform.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, meta has justifiably attracted more scrutiny than ever this year, along with multibillion-dollar judgments and settlements, over how its business practices affect young social media users. The company, however, is not retreating.

In fact, the tech giant has made a major push toward drawing teenagers to one of its flagship platforms, Instagram, by targeting them at their schools.

According to documents obtained and reported by NPR, Meta released an initiative called Project Gryffindor, named after a Hogwarts house in the Harry Potter series, to create school communities on Instagram in order to boost user counts and engagement on the platform.

Recent findings suggest that meta’s goal of approaching young users where they spend the most time offline was not a secret. As recently as late September, the company mentioned it was expanding its School Partnership Program, which includes 17,000 schools, with a stated goal to “help students and parents stay informed.”.

The tech giant’s internal documents reveal some of the motivations behind Meta’s push for school adoption and Project Gryffindor’s proposed features, such as school banners on teen profiles and the ability to search school directories by class year. The details were acquired as part of discovery in a multistate lawsuit over whether social media platforms are designed to be addictive to users under 18. Meta is a defendant in the case, along with other companies, including TikTok, Snap and Google.

In 2024, Instagram introduced Teen accounts and has since been trying to assure parents they’re safe while rolling out additional protections. Studies, however, have suggested that young teens regularly encounter unsafe content or deal with unwanted contact. Recruiting more consumers at an early age without resolving these risks could make teens more vulnerable to mental health challenges and increase the chances of being bullied or harassed.

A representative for Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

In a recent development, to anyone familiar with Meta’s long history of privacy oversteps on platforms like Facebook, the documents aren’t surprising. They reveal a company primed to give school-age children upcoming ways to chat and connect with each other, and to encourage them to bring their friends along, expanding Instagram’s user base and engagement.

Like other social platforms, Instagram primarily makes its money from targeted advertising. User retention is a key part of Meta’s strategy.

In one of the document slides, titled “Why schools, why now?” which preceded Gryffindor’s launch, Meta said, “Competitors are exploring school social use cases, but IG may be better positioned for school connections thanks to our differentiator of meeting new people and building relationships with acquaintances.” In other words, Instagram’s size and scale, with about 3 billion active users globally, automatically make it a draw for students.

The NPR report comes within a week of a filing against Meta alleging that it’s withholding evidence in a major case involving social media’s effects on teenagers.

Industry observers note that one of Meta’s marketing pitches for its School Partnership Program is that it’s trying to create online safe spaces for students, while giving parents and schools more oversight on what’s accessible on the platform. But experts warn that Meta’s history makes it hard to trust the manufacturer with protecting kids from predators or scammers.

Katie Paul, director of the Center for Accountability’s Tech Transparency Project, which has been researching how Meta handles child-safety issues, remarked that Instagram Teen accounts “are not safe as advertised” and that nothing is “legally requiring the company to make these safe.” Paul pointed out that Instagram introduced these accounts only when lawsuits over social media harm started rolling in.

Sources indicate that “It’s all part of a broader marketing (effort) to claim that these are just safer for kids because they are Teen accounts,” Paul said. That marketing effort has included paid endorsements from therapists, psychologists and parent influencers to promote Teen accounts. The case for building up partnerships with schools is a way of “passing the buck on responsibility” to schools and parents, Paul said.

It has been revealed that parents, in particular, have less power in Instagram’s school groups: Unlike the school administrators tasked with managing school groups, parents have no powers to moderate or manage those groups; they can only view them. For Teen accounts in general, parents can’t view direct messages sent to or received by their children.

Industry observers note that meta’s business interests in its push for student engagement and school partnerships are easy to see through. Because kids are likely to be lifetime customers on these platforms, getting them hooked early has long-term financial value.

“Ultimately, Meta is the one profiting off of the data collection of these kids while simultaneously failing to keep them safe,” Paul said.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Uber has opened its ride-hailing service to children as young as 10 in three U.S.
  • The program, which builds on Uber’s existing teen ride-hailing service for passengers ages 13 to 17, is the latest bid by Uber to expand its customer base.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Uber Kids program is stacked with mandatory requirements for parents and drivers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Uber has opened its ride-hailing service to children as young as 10 in three U.S. cities as the manufacturer tests whether there’s a market for shuttling tweens without an adult by their side. The program, called Uber Kids, debuted quietly over the past few weeks in Austin, Texas, Nashville, Tennessee, and Madison, Wisconsin.

The program, which builds on Uber’s existing teen ride-hailing service for passengers ages 13 to 17, is the latest bid by Uber to expand its customer base. Uber is describing this as a limited pilot program, which means it may never expand beyond these cities or even exist by next year. But if successful, it could open up a potentially lucrative market for Uber: busy families with active kids.

Recent findings suggest that the Uber Kids program is stacked with mandatory requirements for parents and drivers. Parents or guardians are the only ones who can order a ride for their child, which they can do by adding the child to their family profile and completing a mandatory onboarding that explains the built-in safety features. A parent or guardian must be present at the pickup locations for the trip to begin and also have to include a note to the driver that explains the drop off.

Meanwhile, only highly rated drivers who have been invited are allowed to participate. Those drivers are required to complete an education module that includes step-by-step instructions and must be opted into live video streaming so parents can watch the trip in real time, according to Uber.

Uber remarked it also requires PIN verification for every Uber Kids trip, and says all recordings will be encrypted and not available to the driver, and will use sensors and GPS data to detect if the ride goes off course, stops unexpectedly, or ends early.

It has been revealed that drivers who are willing to adhere to those rules to shuttle kids will get a pay bump for the effort, according to Uber. Eligible drivers will earn $7 more on every Uber Kids trip compared to a standard one, the company says on the dedicated Uber Kids web page. Drivers will receive an extra $20 for the first Uber Kids ride they complete.

Industry observers note that the extra compensation underscores a key challenge Uber faces as it expands into this younger age group — how to convince drivers to take on that added responsibility. If the program does expand it could eventually compete with existing transportation services such as HopSkipDrive and Zum.

Uber opened its ride-hailing service to minors in 2023 when it launched Uber for Teens, although the organization had conducted early pilots several years prior. As the program expanded nationwide, Uber introduced a live video streaming feature.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Maine's Gambling Control Unit is heading toward an early 2027 launch of tribal-run online casinos after a single public hearing.
  • Maine’s regulator is moving toward an early 2027 launch of tribal-run online casinos.
  • Maine will become the eighth state with legal online casinos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Maine's Gambling Control Unit is heading toward an early 2027 launch of tribal-run online casinos after a single public hearing. A former lawmaker warns that the state's behavioral health system is too thin for a possible rise in gambling addiction, while a federal lawsuit still targets the tribes' exclusivity.

Maine’s regulator is moving toward an early 2027 launch of tribal-run online casinos. Only one public hearing has been held so far. WGME’s I-Team reported on Nov. 16 that the Gambling Control Unit began iGaming rulemaking in June. Residents in the report raised a separate concern. They worry the state lacks the mental health and problem-gambling resources to cope.

Maine will become the eighth state with legal online casinos. Its four Wabanaki tribes hold exclusive licenses under LD 1164, the Wabanaki internet gaming act. The Legislature lists the measure as enacted as Public Law 538.

The money set aside for addiction services is small next to the state’s cut. The legislative fiscal note sends 2% of adjusted gross iGaming receipts to the Gambling Addiction Prevention and Treatment Fund. The state’s own 18% share is projected at $1.8 million in fiscal 2025-26 and $3.6 million in fiscal 2026-27.

Sources indicate that critics doubt the system can absorb the demand. Patty Locuratolo Hymanson, a neurologist and former state lawmaker, told WGME that Maine lacks the behavioral health resources to handle a possible rise in gambling addiction from online casinos.

In a recent development, lawmakers reshaped the revenue split before passage. A committee amendment raised the state’s share from 16% to 18%. The same amendment cut the opioid treatment fund’s allocation from 3% to 1.5%. The fiscal note also carries ongoing General Fund appropriations of $645,354 for six Gambling Control Unit positions. Those include two criminal intelligence analysts and two auditors.

Sources indicate that the regulator itself was skeptical at first. Before the bill became law, Executive Director Milt Champion opposed it in written testimony. He argued iGaming wasn’t warranted while sports wagering was only in its second year.

According to recent reports, rulemaking is still underway. The unit issued its third version of the draft rules on Sept. 30, 2026, and took comments until Oct. 30. Champion has warned that major revisions would force a fourth publication. The third draft keeps the tax rate on adjusted gross receipts unchanged. It also retains the license fee and bond requirements. The regulator is hiring six staff members dedicated to iGaming.

In a recent development, the launch also faces a court fight over tribal exclusivity. Churchill Downs and Oxford Casino Hotel brought their suit against the Gambling Control Unit and Champion in the U.S. District Court for the District of Maine. They are asking the court to declare the law unconstitutional. The challenge goes to the heart of the market’s design, which reserves online casino licenses for the tribes.

The next deadlines are procedural. Under Maine’s rulemaking law, the unit has up to 120 days after comments close to adopt the rules. The Attorney General’s office has up to 150 days from that same date to approve them as legal. The unit’s rulemaking page also lists a public hearing notice marked Nov. 30, 2026, which could change that timetable.

Words can be made from linked letters — up, down, left, right, or diagonal, but words can also change direction, resulting in quirky shapes and patterns. Every single letter in the grid will be part of an answer. By providing an opaque hint and not providing the word list, Strands creates a brain-teasing game that takes a little longer to play than its other games, like Wordle and Connections.

Sources indicate that hey Siri, what’s the name of this blue plant on my screen? You couldn’t ask your iPad that question before, but you’ll be able to soon.

According to recent reports, in its newly introduced iPadOS 27.3 release, Apple is adding several new features for iPads — Siri mode in the camera app, window resizing by tapping and more tools in the Freeform whiteboard app. The features are being tested in beta and will be released to the general public sometime in December. The new OS will be available on all iPads that support iPadOS 27.

The release notes for iPadOS 27.3 are listed here.

Industry observers note that on an iPhone, you can ask Siri about what’s in your camera frame. Siri can identify the object and perform a web search on it. You can also take action items, such as pointing the camera at a restaurant bill and asking Siri to split it if you want to split it with people you’re with.

That same functionality will soon be available on iPads, with the iPadOS 27.3 release. Maybe you want to identify a plant out in nature, or an historic building during a walking tour, or figure out how to replicate a tasty dish you just ordered at a restaurant.

Another fresh feature in iPadOS 27.3 will make it easier to make windows bigger. Let’s say you’ve got a few windows open on your iPad, but there’s one you want to enlarge. You’ll be able to double-tap the top of the window to enlarge it, then double-tap again to revert it to its original size.

Prior to the iPadOS 27.3 release, you had to drag a corner of the window to make it bigger or smaller.

Freeform is an iPad app that serves as a digital whiteboard for sketching and writing out ideas and collaborating. You can add photos, videos, text, PDFs and other items to the whiteboard — using your mouse, finger or Apple Pencil — and sync it across other Apple devices such as iPhones and Macs.

These tech outages are giving Y2K, AI agent style

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (982 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it’s going down, as the American rapper Yung Joc might say: the airline booking systems, banking platforms, and productivity platforms.
  • Sources indicate that apple Pay went down.
  • In a recent development, the first thought, naturally, is an AI hacker invasion of some sort, especially after hackers managed to attack fridges in a grocery store and a blood bank in France a few weeks ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it’s going down, as the American rapper Yung Joc might say: the airline booking systems, banking platforms, and productivity platforms. In the past two weeks, the U.S.’s top businesses have faced technical outages that have disrupted the systems that run everyday life.

Sources indicate that apple Pay went down. NASA’s internal communication network went down. The FAA had to ground all flights for hours (only the third time in history since 9/11), and Microsoft was hit with an outage that took down Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for nearly two days.

In a recent development, the first thought, naturally, is an AI hacker invasion of some sort, especially after hackers managed to attack fridges in a grocery store and a blood bank in France a few weeks ago. Here in the U.S., the director of National Intelligence mentioned these outages don’t seem related to state-sponsored terrorism, while President Trump called the complications “individual events.” Many of the companies themselves have said the outages were not caused by cyberattacks or AI attacks, but tech issues.

Only, there’s the fact that they all struck within a short timespan of each other, and just a few weeks after Cybersecurity’s so-called “Black October,” when a slew of also-unrelated cybersecurity incidents occurred on October 21, striking PHP, Node.js, LiteLLM, more.

While there’s no reason to view these outages as cyberattacks, there may be more than coincidence going on: It’s giving AI-native Y2K, frankly.

Dave DeWalt, an investor who worked in cybersecurity for more than three decades (including as president and CEO of McAfee and as vice chairman of the CISA Advisory Council for the Department of Homeland Security), also thinks it’s probably AI-related.

The technical outages are most likely the “growing pains of a security system that’s getting stronger, not weaker,” and that “AI is surfacing vulnerabilities at a speed and scale we’ve never had before through AI tools like Mythos and others,” he told TechCrunch.

The thing is, many of these technical flaws have always existed, but because AI is surfacing them so fast, enterprises are rushing to fix them before bad actors can exploit them. “That surge in patching is disrupting things in the short term,” he stated.

This was, perhaps, the first moment when legacy meets modern, Anusha Iyer, a software engineer and founder of the security startup Corsha, told TechCrunch. “These industrial systems were never designed to be connected, let alone securely connected in the way we are pushing them to be today,” she said.

Sources indicate that virginia Senator Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intel Committee, came to a similar conclusion (although investigations are still underway as to what could be happening). “These disruptions should serve as a wake-up call. It feels like every day brings another reminder that AI is moving faster than our ability to manage its consequences,” the senator wrote on X.

Sources indicate that AI is reshaping how software is built, deployed, and operated, on a scale where everyone feels the sharp learning curve. Iyer cited the FAA outage as an example of legacy tech that is not as sophisticated or advanced as the technologies companies are trying to merge it with.

In less technical terms, she remarked the outage may have been caused (and preliminary findings point to this) when the FAA was trying to modernize its telecommunications infrastructure and the transition overwhelmed parts of its legacy hardware, where the latest tech likely operated at a normal modern capacity while the legacy hardware couldn’t keep up.

Recent findings suggest that when looked at this way, she mentioned, AI is actually getting the bad rep. “It’s not rapid adoption of AI yet causing these outages,” she said. “The fault is the rushed mix of the legacy and modern systems without a clear understanding of operational and cyber risk or the ability to gatekeep and protect the legacy systems.”.

Organizations need a more steadfast approach to AI adoption, including more testing and prioritizing what needs to be fixed and when, DeWalt remarked.

Iyer added, “These industrial systems need to be segmented more tightly and more access controlled, so as modern systems are introduced, it can be phased in and risk mitigated.”.

Actually, there might be a silver lining to all of this for companies (and for venture investors). DeWalt mentioned he’d rather see these U.S. enterprises find and patch their flaws, even in this messy way, than have bad actors find and exploit those vulnerabilities in AI warfare that could cause even more national security issues.

Sources indicate that and maybe some aspiring founders were inspired by them. DeWalt expects a rise in companies focused on “AI-driven vulnerability management, autonomous remediation, safe patch testing and deployment, and resilience for the systems that keep critical infrastructure running,” he said.

“There’s real pain in this transition as we’ve seen in the past week,” DeWalt stated. “But there’s also enormous opportunity for the companies that help organizations move at AI speed without breaking things.”.

It has been revealed that vector vs. bitmap rendering: Older Android emoji used 2D vector graphics, which scale infinitely to any size without losing resolution. The 3D emoji are bitmap graphics, which are pre-rendered pixel-based images. When these images are scaled up by an app or zoomed in, the pixels stretch, which can cause a softer or lower-resolution appearance.

After the better part of 7 years, Samsung’s mobile division has a upcoming chief and it’s Choi Won-Joon, who is already off to a great start with the successful launch of Galaxy Z Fold 8.

It has been revealed that in an announcement today, Samsung confirmed some shuffling of its executive team, most notably with the end of TM Roh’s tenure as the head of Samsung’s MX business unit. In other words, there’s a new captain at the helm for Samsung’s mobile division, and it’s Choi Won-Joon.

Won-Joon has been the Chief Operating Officer of Samsung’s MX unit since March of 2025, and more recently oversaw the launch of Galaxy S26 and Galaxy Z Fold 8, appearing on stage at both launch events and in behind-the-scenes meetings with the press.

Choi Won-joon, Head of the MX Business Unit at Samsung Electronics’ DX Division, has held positions such as Head of the Next-Generation Product Development Team, Head of the Strategic Product Development Team, and Head of Development at the MX Business Unit. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, as people across the world sneak a day away from the office to play the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto 6 on Thursday, the Rockstar employees who made the game are hopefully enjoying a well-earned day off in celebration.
  • For the 34 workers based in the UK and Canada who Rockstar dismissed in October 2025, GTA 6 launch day isn’t the day of celebration it should’ve been.
  • “I should be with my team, taking a photo at every poster I can see, and be happy about it,” notes Branimira Yordanova, who worked for three years in the lighting department at Rockstar North in Edinburgh, Scotland.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, as people across the world sneak a day away from the office to play the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto 6 on Thursday, the Rockstar employees who made the game are hopefully enjoying a well-earned day off in celebration. But not everyone who worked on the cultural juggernaut is joining the victory lap.

For the 34 workers based in the UK and Canada who Rockstar dismissed in October 2025, GTA 6 launch day isn’t the day of celebration it should’ve been.

“I should be with my team, taking a photo at every poster I can see, and be happy about it,” notes Branimira Yordanova, who worked for three years in the lighting department at Rockstar North in Edinburgh, Scotland. “But it’s impossible because of how much hurt the firing has caused everyone.”.

Rockstar fired the workers on the spot — something that’s only legal in the UK in cases of gross misconduct — alleging that they’d shared confidential firm information on a Discord server.

In a recent development, the workers tell a different story. They say the tech giant had long been aware of the Discord server, and only fired them when it started to look as though their efforts to unionize might succeed. They believe they were made an example of.

On the evening before the game’s launch, I spoke with Yordanova and her former colleague Dayne Oram, a senior production coordinator who had been at Rockstar North for seven years and was also affected by the dismissals, about how they were feeling about launch day.

“One of our fellow colleagues remarked it the best,” says Yordanova. “What we’ll feel tomorrow is mourning what could have been, whether we want to or not.”.

For all those who are mourning, others among the fired workers still hold a candle for GTA. Jacob Jones, who spent one year as a game tester before taking a role as a designer on the open world team for four years, was raring to play the game on launch day.

It has been revealed that jones graduated from being a childhood fan of the franchise – even counting the signatures of Rockstar co-founders Sam and Dan Hauser among his merch collection – to his dream job. He remains a GTA fan to this day, but describes feeling a sense of “poignance” and “bittersweetness” toward the launch.

For Oram, Yordanova and Jones, GTA 6 eve was already a heavy day, even aside from the launch fever.

Recent findings suggest that they’re all part of a case brought by the Independent Workers’ Union of Great Britain on behalf of 23 former Rockstar North employees, who say they were unfairly dismissed for union activity. Hours before Oram and Yordanova spoke with me, a Glasgow employment tribunal had heard Rockstar’s closing submissions, which now leaves the fired workers in limbo as they wait for a verdict.

Rockstar North maintains that it fired the employees for gross misconduct. The company didn’t respond to a request for further comment.

Oram, Yordanova and Jones all speak highly of their former colleagues and teams, but Oram calls the sacking a “traumatic experience.” None have managed to secure alternative employment in the past 13 months. Jones claims for now he’s focused on getting justice.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, reminders of their former employer have been everywhere as the studio geared up to release perhaps the most highly anticipated game of all time. Billboards, buses and online ads have been impossible to avoid, leaving Yordanova feeling “devastated.”.

According to recent reports, “I’ve genuinely had to make sure to avoid looking at it,” she notes. “It’s such a cool game, and to know that you worked on it, you feel a sense of pride and joy to see it out. But it’s like that sense of joy has been taken away from us in such a ruthless manner.”.

Recent findings suggest that oram acknowledges having “mixed feelings” about the launch. It’s been fantastic watching video footage of people playing and reviewing the game, they say. At the same time, they’ve found it difficult not being able to celebrate the moment with their former team.

It has been revealed that the workers fired from Rockstar North had varying ideas about whether they wanted to celebrate the launch, or avoid it entirely. Jones is one of those who started playing the game as soon as he got home from the tribunal at 1 a.m. By the time we spoke on Thursday, he’d played around six or seven hours.

“I personally think it’s a masterpiece,” he says. Even though he worked on the game, he’s discovering surprises everywhere. “I haven’t completed it yet, but I do think it is probably the greatest game ever made.”.

Oram notes that they planned to stick with watching streams of the game on launch day. “I’m probably not going to play the game for a little while, but I am looking forward to at least watching some people,” they say. Oram worked across so many bits of the game that there’s plenty they’re excited to see people discover.

Sources indicate that yordanova says she’s firmly in the avoidance camp. “I was really excited about playing the game in its official form because obviously when you work on it, you get to play it,” she says. “Even while we were in the office, there were parts I was really excited about – but I don’t think I’ll be playing it for the foreseeable future.”.

Industry observers note that she hopes that one day her feelings will change, she adds. “But right now, that’s just not possible in any way.”.

According to recent reports, instead, she’ll be spending the day with friends who supported her over the last year. She plans to “dive into another art form” by seeing the stop-motion animated film Wildwood at the cinema, which particularly appeals to her as a lighting artist.

Many people playing GTA 6 around the world won’t be aware of what happened to Oram, Yordanova, Jones and their colleagues during the game’s development, but the affected workers would like people to know. “I understand people just want to focus on the joy, but I don’t think you can separate the launch with what happened,” claims Yordanova.

Reflecting on what happened, Jones claims it’s such a shame the way things went down. “It was my absolute passion,” he says. “I just wish that the circumstances were different, and I would have loved to have still been there working on games. I wish I got to the end.”.

Meta aims to charge $300 for Muse Charm, its upcoming Tamagotchi-like AI device that was teased at the organization’s Connect event earlier this year, The Information has reported.

When reached for comment by TechCrunch, a Meta spokesperson didn’t deny the claims, merely providing the following statement: “We’re charmed by the interest in our AI devices, and we’ll have more to share soon.”.

So far, Meta has made a relatively successful push into consumer AI, launching Muse — its agentic helper — along with a variety of cute avatars that users can use to give the system more of a personality.

Muse Charm, the company’s push into AI hardware, will allow users to carry a physical personification of its software around in their pocket (or potentially wear it around their neck), talking to it, asking it questions, and giving it commands.

It remains to be seen whether customers will bite or not. AI wearables have had a rough go of it so far (here’s looking at you, Humane Ai pin), but companies continue to iterate on the concept in an attempt to break through to a broader audience.

Indeed, $300 is arguably a pretty steep price for a product the size of a keychain, although it’s also a price point that’s in line with what other companies have been charging. The wearable debuted by Friend — the AI startup whose device lets you text and talk to an AI persona — is currently retailing for $250. On the other hand, Amazon’s all-new Bee Frontier wearable AI device — which transcribes conversations and tracks tasks — lists for $75 and is currently on a Black Friday, 30% off sale of $52.49. Even with its $99/year subscription to let it tie into a user’s apps (photos, emails, etc.), it’s still far less expensive than Muse Charm.

Android's sideloading freedom is about to get a lot more complicated worldwide

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that for quite a long time, Android has had one substantial advantage over iOS: you can install apps from basically anywhere, without asking Google's permission.
  • Google has confirmed that its developer verification requirements will begin rolling out globally in January 2027, making it harder to install apps from developers who haven’t registered with the company.
  • It has been revealed that announced in 2025, the policy requires Android app developers to verify their identities and register their applications with Google, regardless of where those applications are distributed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that for quite a long time, Android has had one substantial advantage over iOS: you can install apps from basically anywhere, without asking Google's permission. That freedom is about to come with considerably more friction.

Google has confirmed that its developer verification requirements will begin rolling out globally in January 2027, making it harder to install apps from developers who haven’t registered with the company.

It has been revealed that announced in 2025, the policy requires Android app developers to verify their identities and register their applications with Google, regardless of where those applications are distributed. The fresh rules will also apply to third-party app marketplaces and independently distributed APKs.

Google is working with seven distributors, including Google Play, Samsung’s Galaxy Store, Honor, Oppo, Xiaomi, Transsion, and Vivo, to bring the requirements to more users.

Sources indicate that google states the changes are intended to make it more difficult for scammers and malicious developers to continue distributing harmful apps. The company says millions of applications have already been registered, representing more than 99% of Android app installs worldwide. The launch began on September 30, 2026, in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand.

But developers won’t be the only ones feeling the shift. To install unverified apps, you’ll have to take extra steps. You’ll have to authenticate your device and make sure you’re not being forced to change your security settings. After this, restart your phone and wait 24 hours before you can enable unrestricted sideloading.

Google does offer an advanced install option for power users who want to skip verification, but it’s not quite the one-tap experience Android enthusiasts have grown accustomed to.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

There are also concessions for smaller developers. Free limited-distribution accounts allow students and hobbyists to share apps with up to 50 authorized devices without having to verify their identity with a government ID or pay registration fees. Google has also added APIs to make it easier for developers with multiple apps to register.

In a recent development, but the bigger question is what this change means for Android’s reputation as an open platform. Google says users can still choose where they download their apps from, but the freedom is made a lot less convenient by adding identity checks, restrictions on installation, and a mandatory waiting period.

After the global rollout, protections are expected to be available to all countries and installation sources over the span of a few months. Google documentation states that full enforcement is expected on March 1, 2027.

#2012. Industry News: Want to see your live AI usage on your Mac’s icons? This clever fresh app lets you

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (784 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Want to see your live AI usage on your Mac’s icons? This clever fresh app lets you

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (784 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There’s a fresh way to keep an eye on your AI usage and when your limits reset: by using your Mac’s app icons.
  • Designer Michael Flarup has just launched a new Mac utility called IconSwapper, which lets you replace any app’s official icon with one of your own creation.
  • Doing so is fairly simple, and you don’t have to be technically minded to get this to work.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s a fresh way to keep an eye on your AI usage and when your limits reset: by using your Mac’s app icons. Yes, really!

Designer Michael Flarup has just launched a new Mac utility called IconSwapper, which lets you replace any app’s official icon with one of your own creation. While you can use this tool to change your icons’ appearance, design, shading, and more, one of the more interesting ways to use it is to swap the icons for AI apps like ChatGPT or Claude with versions that can display your live AI usage.

Doing so is fairly simple, and you don’t have to be technically minded to get this to work. After installing the app on your Mac, you simply choose which application you want to create a “live” icon for — meaning one that responds to a particular app.

Besides tracking AI usage in ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor, you can also create live icons for a number of the built-in Mac apps like Messages, Mail, Safari, Finder, Music, and others like Chrome and Spotify, but these configurations tend to be more fun than they are practical. For instance, you can configure Safari’s compass to follow things like page loads and downloads, or you can make it so that the Finder guy’s eyes follow your cursor around the screen. (That one is hilarious!).

Industry observers note that of course, there are plenty of other ways to track your AI usage — you don’t need an icon to do that. You can track usage from your account or your harness, even from a fun little gadget. But tracking it from the icon adds a certain whimsy to your Mac desktop setup. (If your dock is crowded, note that you can also see your icon customizations from your tab bar as you switch apps.).

Beyond live icons, you can also change what an icon looks like using IconSwapper’s built-in tools.

Sources indicate that there are a surprising number of built-in customizations that are as easy to use as clicking a few buttons or toggling a switch. IconSwapper also comes with a large library of alternative icons for every app that are already ready to use, or you can upload your own.

Flarup is based in Copenhagen, where he runs a design studio, and he has been drawn to icon design and customization for years. He’s been making his own Mac icons since the early 2000s and even wrote a book about app icons that celebrates the work of designers.

He had been working on a solution that would allow him to customize Mac icons, which had proven tricky because macOS has no official support for theming and protects its system icons. To work around this, he came up with a different technique that involves drawing directly on the icons without replacing them, allowing him to use shaders, motion, and display real data.

Flarup tells TechCrunch that his renderer runs the icon artwork through custom Metal shaders in real time.

Sources indicate that “The breakthrough was figuring out how to send the Dock a bitmap for another running app and have it draw that frame itself,” he explained. “I spent a lot of time getting the artwork to follow the icon through all the little ways macOS moves it, from Dock magnification to the Command-Tab switcher. Once I had that working, I could make the icon react to whatever’s happening,” Flarup said.

That lets users configure icons to do all kinds of fun, latest things they never could before, like make light move across a gold icon as you drag your cursor over it, or animate an app’s icon while it’s thinking.

In a recent development, “That opens up a lot of fun ways to make your Mac feel like yours. I’ve always felt the software we use every day could be a little more fun and a lot more personal,” he added.

The app itself is a one-time purchase of $19 as a launch promo but will later sell for $29, its website says.
